sentences.text: Hello, everyone. My name is Emili. Welcome to the Slow English podcast. In this podcast,
we speak slow and easy English. Today, we talk about a very special and less known city.
The city is Kiva. Kiva is in Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia. Kiva is an old
city with a long history. Many travelers say Kiva feels like an open museum. The city has
many old buildings and historical places. Part 2. Kiva is more than 1,000 years old. Long ago,
it was an important city on the Silk Road. The Silk Road was a famous trade route. Traders
traveled from China to Europe. They carried silk, spices, and many goods. Kiva was an important
stop for these travelers. Part 3. The old part of Kiva is called Itchonkala. Itchonkala is surrounded
by large walls. These walls protected the city many years ago. The walls are strong and made
of clay and brick. Today, visitors can walk around the old city and see the beautiful buildings.
Part 4. Kiva is famous for its towers called minarets. These tall towers are part of mosques.
One famous minaret is called the Kalta Minor. It is wide and covered with blue and green tiles.
The colors shine in the sunlight. Many tourists take photos of this beautiful tower. Part 5.
The city also has many mosques and madrasas. A madrasa is a school where people study religion
and history. Many of these buildings are very old but still beautiful. They have colorful
tiles and traditional designs. Walking in the city feels like going back in time. Part
6. Kiva is not a very big city. The streets are small and quiet. Many streets are made
of stone. There are old doors, wooden windows, and beautiful walls. Visitors like to walk
slowly and explore the small streets. Part 7. The people of Kiva are friendly and welcoming.
They are proud of their history and culture. Many people work in tourism. They guide visitors
and explain the history of the city. Some people also sell handmade products. Part 8. Markets
in Kiva are colorful and interesting. People sell carpets, hats, and traditional clothes.
Some shops sell handmade pottery and wooden items. These products are made by local artisans.
Visitors often buy souvenirs from the markets. Part 9. Food in Kiva is traditional Uzbek food.
One famous dish is called plav. Plav is rice cooked with meat, carrots, and spices. It is
a popular meal in Uzbekistan. Another common food is bread. Uzbek bread is round and baked in
special ovens. Part 10. The weather in Kiva can be very hot in summer. The city is near the desert.
In winter, the weather can be cold. Spring and autumn are the best seasons to visit.
During these seasons, the temperature is comfortable for walking and exploring.
Part 11. At sunset, Kiva becomes very magical. The sun shines on the clay walls and buildings.
The city becomes golden and beautiful. Many visitors enjoy watching the sunset from the city walls or from the top of a tower.
It is a peaceful and unforgettable moment. Part 12. Kiva is a small city but full of history and beauty.
The old buildings, colorful tiles, and quiet streets make it special.
